title: Selection of the electromagnetic source tensor by covariance, conservation and the exchange law
abstract: On a fixed flat Lorentz frame with metric diag(1,1,1,-1), sources are symmetric 4x4 tensor-valued functions of the six real components of an antisymmetric field. Twelve kernel-checked statements. Among all symmetric homogeneous quadratic sources (210 free coefficients), the six infinitesimal Lorentz covariance equations together with zero trace select the Maxwell stress (the electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor) up to a unique real scale, and a displayed certificate of 209 linear coefficient equations is equivalent to both laws. Among the same homogeneous quadratic sources, conservation alone - vanishing divergence on every source-free Maxwell/Bianchi first jet - selects the same line, with covariance, trace zero and Hodge invariance derived rather than assumed. The globally C^3 symmetric conserved sources are exactly an explicit seventeen-parameter family (constant, a six-parameter cross term, and the stress), and with covariance zero field value is equivalent to zero trace and to the stress line. Under the sourceful exchange law at current stiffness k (the real factor multiplying the jet current), every everywhere-differentiable symmetric source is a constant plus the Maxwell stress of scale exactly k, and conversely, with no polynomial, degree, C^3, covariance or trace hypothesis; zero field value selects the stress. Explicit counterexamples show that covariance and zero trace are each necessary in the quadratic selection, and that covariance and the zero-field normalization are each necessary in the C^3 selection. Uniqueness of the Maxwell stress tensor is classical (Fock 1964; Kerrighan 1982; Navarro-Sancho 2012; the classification of Maxwell conservation laws by Anco-Pohjanpelto 2001); the contribution is the constructive, kernel-checked development on the explicit register at finite regularity, with finite certificates, the covariance-free routes, and the differentiable-only sourceful statement. Pisot Dimensional Theory motivates the frame; no physical coupling is selected.
